title: 15 years, 15 perspectives: How AI will redefine human collaboration
summary: On Zoom's 15th anniversary, CEO Eric Yuan shares his vision for the future of work and how AI will redefine human collaboration.
body_text: Eric founded Zoom in 2011 to deliver happiness and bring people together in a frictionless video environment. Zoom’s communications platform continues to transform the way global organizations connect, communicate, and collaborate. As the company’s chief executive, Eric led Zoom to one of the highest-performing tech IPOs of 2019. Business Insider named Eric one of the Most Powerful People in Enterprise Tech in 2017. In 2018, Glassdoor recognized him as the top CEO for large U.S. companies. In 2019, he was recognized in the Bloomberg 50 as a leader changing the game in global business. Time Magazine named Eric its 2020 Businessperson of Year as well as one of the 100 Most Influential People of 2020. He was also named Comparably's Best CEO for Diversity in 2021. Prior to founding Zoom, Eric was corporate vice president of engineering at Cisco, where he was responsible for Cisco's collaboration software development. Eric was also one of the founding engineers and vice president of engineering at Webex. Eric is a named inventor on 11 issued and 20 pending patents in real-time collaboration.

title: Comprehensive Guide to Mental Health Counselor Training and Certification
summary: SimCare AI creates AI Patients so students can practice counseling skills, explore different scenarios, and get immediate feedback.
body_text: Mental health counselor training is a structured process combining academic coursework, supervised clinical experience, and practical skills development to prepare individuals for professional counseling roles. Integrating advanced tools like AI client simulations and virtual avatars, such as those from SimCare, enhances skill acquisition and confidence beyond traditional methods. Key takeaways Mental health counselor training combines academic study, supervised clinical experience, and practical skill-building for licensure. AI-powered simulations and virtual counseling avatars can accelerate skill development and confidence for counseling students. Licensure as a mental health counselor requires a master’s degree, supervised hours, and passing a national exam. Online training options are increasingly robust, but hands-on practice with tools like SimCare is essential for real-world readiness. Counselors and therapists differ in training and scope; understanding these distinctions is key for career planning. What is mental health counselor training and why is it important? Mental health counselor training is the formal education and supervised practice required to become a competent, ethical counselor. This training is crucial because it ensures counselors can support clients with diverse mental health needs using evidence-based approaches. Training typically includes graduate-level coursework in counseling theories, ethics, assessment, and intervention techniques, along with hands-on clinical experience. Modern programs increasingly incorporate technology, such as virtual patient simulations for counseling students , to provide realistic practice opportunities and immediate feedback. These innovations help bridge the gap between theory and real-world application, ensuring future counselors are well-prepared for the complexities of client care. What are the educational requirements to become a mental health counselor? To become a mental health counselor, most states require at least a master’s degree in counseling, psychology, or a closely related field. Accredited programs must include both classroom instruction and supervised clinical hours. Core coursework covers topics such as counseling techniques, human development, multicultural counseling, and ethics. Supervised practicum and internship experiences are essential, allowing students to apply their knowledge in real settings. For a deeper dive into foundational skills, discover counseling training essentials in our dedicated guide. How do you become a licensed mental health counselor (LMHC)? Becoming a licensed mental health counselor (LMHC) involves completing a master’s degree, accruing supervised clinical hours, and passing a national licensing exam. Each state sets specific requirements, but this pathway is standard across the U.S. After earning a degree, candidates must typically complete 2,000–4,000 hours of post-graduate supervised experience. The National Clinical Mental Health Counseling Examination (NCMHCE) or a state-specific test is required for licensure. Using tools like SimCare’s AI Client Simulations can help trainees prepare for real-world scenarios and licensing assessments. What certifications are available for clinical mental health counselors? Several certifications are available to demonstrate advanced competency in clinical mental health counseling. The most recognized is the National Certified Counselor (NCC) credential from the National Board for Certified Counselors (NBCC). Additional credentials include the Certified Clinical Mental Health Counselor (CCMHC) and specialty certifications in areas like addiction or trauma. These certifications often require additional coursework, supervised experience, and passing a specialty exam. For those interested in substance use counseling, explore how to become a substance abuse counselor for more details. What is the quickest way to become a mental health counselor? The fastest route to becoming a mental health counselor is to enroll in an accredited master’s program with integrated practicum and internship placements, allowing for streamlined completion of educational and clinical requirements. Some programs offer accelerated tracks or allow students to begin supervised hours concurrently with coursework. However, licensure requirements for supervised post-graduate hours and exams are typically fixed by state law. Leveraging AI-powered simulations, like those from SimCare, can help students build skills efficiently and be better prepared for clinical placements and exams. How does online mental health counselor training compare to traditional programs? Online mental health counselor training programs can offer flexibility and accessibility, but must meet the same accreditation and supervised practice standards as in-person programs. The quality of online training depends on interactive components and opportunities for real-world skill application. SimCare’s Virtual Counseling Avatars and Feedback and Performance Analytics enable students in online programs to gain hands-on experience and receive structured feedback, bridging the gap between digital learning and practical skill development. When evaluating online options, ensure the program includes robust opportunities for supervised practice and technology-enhanced learning. Can you become a mental health counselor without a degree? In the United States, a graduate degree is required to become a licensed mental health counselor. There are no pathways to full licensure without completing at least a master’s program from an accredited institution. Some entry-level roles, such as peer support or case management, may be available with a bachelor’s degree or specialized training, but these do not qualify as licensed counseling positions. For those seeking alternative entry points, understand crisis counselor training programs to explore related support roles. What are the typical salaries and career prospects for mental health counselors? Mental health counselors in the U.S. earn a median annual wage of $49,710 as of 2023, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. Salaries vary by region, specialization, and experience level. Demand for mental health counselors is expected to increase in the coming years, much faster than the average for all occupations. Career prospects are strong in settings such as schools, healthcare facilities, private practice, and community agencies. Tools like Session Scheduling and Progress Tracking can help counselors manage growing caseloads and monitor client outcomes. How do mental health counselors differ from therapists? Mental health counselors and therapists both provide talk-based interventions, but differ in training, licensure, and scope of practice. Mental health counselors typically hold an LMHC or LPC license, focusing on practical, solution-oriented therapy, while therapists may include psychologists, social workers, or marriage and family therapists with different educational backgrounds and licensure. The table below summarizes key differences: Role Typical Degree Licensure Primary Focus Mental Health Counselor (LMHC/LPC) Master’s in Counseling LMHC/LPC Individual, group, and family counseling Therapist (e.g., Psychologist, LCSW, LMFT) Master’s or Doctorate Varies (LCSW, LMFT, PhD, PsyD) Broader mental health assessment and therapy Understanding these distinctions helps students choose the right training path for their career goals. What specialized training options exist for mental health counselors? Specialized training for mental health counselors includes advanced coursework, certifications, and technology-enhanced practice. AI-powered simulations, such as those developed by SimCare, allow students to engage with lifelike virtual clients in over 500 customizable scenarios, supporting skill development in areas like crisis intervention, trauma, and multicultural counseling. Faculty and program directors can use these tools to standardize student practice, observe sessions, and provide structured feedback. For a comprehensive overview of practical training options, review our course catalog for skills and topics available for simulation-based practice. Frequently Asked Questions What is the quickest way to become a mental health counselor? The quickest way is to complete an accredited master’s program with integrated practicum and internship placements, followed by required supervised hours and passing the licensing exam. How do you become a mental health counselor? You can pursue a diploma, degree, or postgraduate course in counseling or psychotherapy, often alongside subjects like psychology or sociology. Look for programs with practical skills training and supervised placements. Is a LMHC the same as a therapist? An LMHC is a type of therapist, but not all therapists are LMHCs. Therapists may hold various licenses, such as psychologist, LCSW, or LMFT, each with distinct training and scope. What degree do most mental health counselors have? Most mental health counselors hold a master’s degree in counseling, psychology, or a closely related field from an accredited program. References National Certified Counselor (NCC) Credential – NBCC Certified Clinical Mental Health Counselor (CCMHC) – NBCC

title: Experience Agent 1.0: One agent for every participant
summary: At LDT Live, we unveiled Experience Agent 1.0, our first agent built for participants. Here's what it can do and how it works in practice.
body_text: At LDT Live, we unveiled Experience Agent 1.0, our first agent built for participants. Chris Saunders from the Experience team took the stage to show what it can do and how it works in practice. For those who missed it, here's a walkthrough: Purpose-built for endurance sports We've heard from many of our partners that participant support, particularly in the weeks around race day, can be a real challenge. Thousands of questions arrive, sometimes in different languages and across time zones, and every one of them needs a considered response. Even a well-staffed support team can find itself spending most of race week on the same handful of queries, year after year. This is where the Experience Agent steps in. Simply give it your branding, point it at your event website, and it's ready to go live, available around the clock, responding in whatever language a participant writes in. There's no separate knowledge base to set up or maintain. When your site changes, the agent keeps pace automatically. In practice, that means questions your team would normally field every year get handled without them lifting a finger. It means a participant dealing with an injury days before race day gets a response that sounds human, not like a policy document. And it means your dashboard gives you a clear view of what people are actually asking about and where gaps in your content exist. Accuracy matters here, so we've focused on giving you clear visibility into what the agent can answer confidently and where it needs more information to do so. The hours your team used to spend on repeat queries through race week are freed up for the conversations that actually need them. If the agent doesn't know an answer, it won't guess - it hands straight off to your team, so you stay in control of anything that calls for a personal touch. In early deployments, the Experience Agent is resolving 85% of conversations without human support, with a 93% participant satisfaction score. Reccently, one participant rang the Run 4 Wales team, who are using the agent, not to raise a complaint but to say how much they'd enjoyed talking it. Shaped by our event organizers A big thank you to the organisers who gave early feedback and helped shape Experience Agent into what it is today. We can't wait to get these capabilities into your hands. "The Experience Agent is working really well — we're so pleased with it. We even had a call to the office to say it was the best AI agent they'd dealt with." - Lee Treadwell, Head of Marketing & Communications, R4W Want to see Nova in action for yourself? title: Ferrovial appoints John L. Morton as CEO of the Airports division
summary: Sala de prensa Ferrovial | Últimas noticias
body_text: Ferrovial has appointed John L. Morton as CEO of the Airports division , effective September 2026. He will succeed Luke Bugeja, who will retire from his role after more than five years of successful contribution to the company. “I am pleased to welcome John to Ferrovial’s Management Committee. His extensive experience in transportation infrastructure, aviation, and public-private partnerships will be instrumental as we continue to strengthen Ferrovial Airports and deliver long-term value for our stakeholders,” said Ignacio Madridejos, CEO of Ferrovial. “I would also like to thank Luke for his leadership and dedication over the past five years and wish him all the best in his retirement.” Prior to joining Ferrovial, John L. Morton was Managing Director of Global Infrastructure Partners (part of Blackrock), where he established and led the Transportation team in the Americas. He also served as Director of Investment Banking for Credit Suisse in London and New York. Morton holds a B.A. in Psychology and a Certificate in Marketing and Management from Duke University and holds an MBA degree from the London Business School. Luke Bugeja has committed to stay in the company until his retirement in November to support a smooth transition to John L. Morton.

title: CHIPOTLE PUTS A NEW TWIST ON SOCCER'S HYDRATION BREAK WITH $1 MILLION IN FREE BURRITOS
summary: During the second official hydration break of this summer's international tournament final on July 19, Chipotle will launch its first-ever Chipotle "Water" Break, giving viewers a chance to unlock...
body_text: During the second official hydration break of this summer's international tournament final on July 19, Chipotle will launch its first-ever Chipotle "Water" Break, giving viewers a chance to unlock entrée offers Inspired by Chipotle's iconic water cups and the playful conversation surrounding guests who "accidentally" fill them with lemonade, the activation will challenge participants to track a lemonade-filled cup on the @Chipotle Instagram NEWPORT BEACH, Calif. , July 16, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- Chipotle Mexican Grill (NYSE: CMG) today announced that it is turning one of soccer's newest matchday traditions into a $1 million burrito giveaway inspired by the long-running social conversation surrounding its iconic water cups. During the international tournament final on July 19, viewers at home can participate in a Chipotle "Water" Break for a chance to unlock free entrée offers. When play pauses for the match's second official hydration break, Chipotle will bring a stadium-inspired game to fans watching from home. The brand will share a video from the @Chipotle Instagram account challenging viewers to follow a lemonade-filled cup as three identical Chipotle water cups shuffle across the screen. At the end of the video, the lemonade-filled cup will reveal a text-to-win code. The first 100,000 participants to text the code to 888-222 will receive a free entrée offer.¹ Some Chipotle fans have been known to "accidentally" fill their complimentary water cups with lemonade at the beverage station. Over the years, Chipotle has leaned into the joke, acknowledging these "accidents" in a series of self-aware posts on social media (see HERE , HERE , HERE ). "The best brand ideas start with a fan truth," said Stephanie Perdue, Senior Vice President, Marketing at Chipotle. "Our water cup has become one of the most recognizable symbols in Chipotle fan culture, and when hydration breaks emerged as a new part of the matchday experience, we saw an opportunity to bring that fan lore to life on one of the biggest stages in sports." A Summer of Soccer and Burritos The Chipotle "Water" Break builds on the success of last month's Matchday BOGO, which became the biggest promotional day in company history. Chipotle's jersey BOGOs have become a fan-favorite tradition, with guests showing their pride in everything from official jerseys to homemade creations just for the occasion (see HERE , HERE , HERE ). This summer's tournament has also introduced Chipotle to international visitors traveling across North America, many of whom are experiencing iconic American brands and traditions for the first time. From longtime Chipotle superfans to first-time guests discovering the brand during their travels, the activation gives everyone another way to celebrate the conclusion of the summer's biggest sporting event. 1 — Free Entrée codes will be valid for any regularly priced entrée, subject to availability, until 7/24/26. Valid in the U.S. only, 13+. Standard text & data rates may apply. Additional terms: chipotle.com/water-break. ABOUT CHIPOTLE Chipotle Mexican Grill, Inc. (NYSE: CMG) is cultivating a better world by serving responsibly sourced, classically-cooked, real food with wholesome ingredients without artificial colors, flavors or preservatives. There are over 4,100 restaurants as of March 31, 2026, in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, France, Germany, and the Middle East and it is the only restaurant company of its size that owns and operates all its restaurants in North America and Europe. With over 135,000 employees passionate about providing a great guest experience, Chipotle is a longtime leader and innovator in the food industry. Chipotle is committed to making its food more accessible to everyone while continuing to be a brand with a demonstrated purpose as it leads the way in digital, technology and sustainable business practices. For more information or to place an order online, visit Chipotle.com . SOURCE Chipotle Mexican Grill
